panels.description: How long each problem pod has been alive (time since pod creation). Combined with restart count this helps decide priority: short duration + few restarts = likely transient; long duration or many restarts = needs attention.
panels.title: Problem Pods - Duration (since pod creation)

panels.description: Last termination reason for each container of a problem pod. Tells you WHY without checking logs: OOMKilled = memory issue, Error = app crash, Completed = job finished normally. Pending pods that never ran will not appear here.

defaults.noValue: No terminated containers among problem pods

panels.title: Problem Pods - Last Termination Reason

panels.description: Exit code of the last terminated container for each problem pod. Read alongside Last Reason: 137 = SIGKILL (128+9) which can mean OOMKilled, node-pressure eviction, or a liveness-probe kill; 143 = SIGTERM (graceful); 0 = clean exit; 1/2 = application error. The code alone is ambiguous - the reason column disambiguates it.

defaults.noValue: No terminated containers among problem pods

panels.description: Pods that have restarted more than 10 times in the last 2 hours. These services may currently look Running (healthy), but the high restart rate indicates an underlying problem: memory leaks (OOMKilled), recurring crashes, or failing liveness probes. Empty = no flapping services found, which is the expected healthy state.
